//: Rosetta binding manifest for the Geogram library.
//paths: All relative paths resolve from THIS file's directory (the project root).
//design: GEO::Mesh is bound DIRECTLY, and so are its member objects: mesh.vertices / mesh.facets / mesh.facet_corners are member-object reference properties (non-copyable stores holding a Mesh& back-reference; 'final': true suppresses their trampolines — MeshVertices/MeshFacets have public virtuals — which is also what lets node alias them). Geometry moves through geogram's own API: vertices.assign_points / facets.assign_triangle_mesh / vertices.point_coordinates, whose GEO::vector<T> parameters marshal as flat script arrays via the 'sequences' trait (their raw-pointer overloads are declared second, so the walk keeps the sequence one). There is no glue left AT ALL: triangles() is mesh.facets.triangulate() (geogram fan-triangulates identically — mesh.cpp) followed by mesh.facet_corners.vertex_indices(), and tex_coords() is mesh.facet_corners.attributes().get_doubles('tex_coord'), whose two written-through references are declared out-parameters below. load()/save() are Mesh members upstream (non-overloaded, PR #373) and bind natively, like copy/clear/show_stats. The GEO:: algorithms (remesh, repair, Co3Ne reconstruction, atlas, intersections, booleans) are bound straight from their headers, the overloaded ones through an explicit 'signature'; CSG is GEO::CSGCompiler bound as a class. src/ is GONE — the binding is geogram's own API, end to end. geogram's lifecycle (GEO::initialize + the seven CmdLine::import_arg_group calls + routing OpenNL's printf through the Logger) now runs from 'module_init' when the module loads, and <geogram/version.h> comes from 'generated_headers' instead of a checked-in stand-in. NOTE: rosetta does not capture C++ default arguments — every parameter is explicit in the bindings.
//sources: The geogram sources are compiled straight into every binding target (no prebuilt libgeogram: the wasm target needs the sources anyway, and a native lib built by another toolchain would risk an ABI mismatch). One glob per source dir, DELIBERATELY not the recursive ** — the set is selective: geogram/lua/, geogram/api/ and most of third_party/ (tetgen, triangle, PoissonRecon, stb, amgcl, lua) must stay out. The vendored zlib/rply/libMeshb/OpenNL are C sources (the generated projects enable_language(C)).
//defaults: The top-level namespace default qualifies every unqualified class/function name with GEO:: (georo::* spellings pass verbatim). Groups ({"header": ..., "entries": [...]}) scope a shared header over a run of entries.
//defines: GEOGRAM_USE_BUILTIN_DEPS: mesh_io/geofile include the vendored libMeshb/rply/zlib instead of system libs. GEOGRAM_WITH_HLBFGS: compiles the HLBFGS optimizer in (required by the Newton iterations of CVT remeshing).
//link-options: Under Node, geogram's GEO::initialize() mounts the host filesystem with NODEFS (EM_ASM in basic/common.cpp), so the wasm link needs emscripten's nodefs.js library — exactly what geogram's own cmake/platforms/Emscripten-clang.cmake adds.
//sequences: GEO::vector<T> marshals like std::vector<T> (flat script arrays) through rosetta's sequence adapters — this is what lets geogram's own assign_points / assign_triangle_mesh bind (their GEO::vector overload is declared first, so it survives the walk's overload dedup and the adapter resolves the call by name). Mutable GEO::vector& parameters bind input-only (steal_arg steals from the adapter's copy, which is fine).
//module-init: geogram's LIFECYCLE, run when the module loads — this is what georo::initialize() used to be. GEO::initialize registers the mesh I/O handlers mesh.load()/save() need; the argument groups are where the algorithms read their tuning parameters from; nlPrintfFuncs routes OpenNL's printf/fprintf through geogram's Logger (as CmdLine::parse does in geogram's own programs) so solver output honors the quiet flag. Quiet by default. GEO::Logger cannot be bound to expose the switch — it derives from Counted and its destructor is protected, which no backend can wrap — so flip the set_quiet(true) statement below and regenerate to get geogram's log output.
//generated-headers: <geogram/version.h> is generated by geogram's own CMake from version.h.in; geogram-rosetta compiles the sources without running that CMake, so rosetta writes it here — from geogram's own template, so there is no second copy to keep in sync. GEOGRAM_VERSION is passed with -D by geogram's CMake (basic/common.cpp reads it), which is what the compile_definitions entry below is.
//out-params: Which parameters a function RETURNS through a reference. Never inferred, and this manifest is why: GEO::MeshVertices::assign_points takes its GEO::vector<double>& as an INPUT it steals from, while AttributesManager::get_doubles fills its own as an OUTPUT — the same C++ shape, opposite directions. Marked here, get_doubles(name, out, dim) exposes get_doubles(name) returning (ok, values, dim).

classes.//: --- the mesh and its member-object stores ---

--- the attribute store behind mesh.facet_corners.attributes(). get_doubles is the read path for the UVs mesh_make_atlas writes: its GEO::vector<double>& and index_t& are OUT-parameters (see out_params), so scripts get (ok, values, dim) back instead of passing anything in. ---
classes.name: AttributesManager

classes.//: --- CSG: bound directly. compile_file's std::filesystem::path marshals as a string and both compile_* return std::shared_ptr<Mesh>, which every target now handles (python holder, embind smart_ptr, sol2 native, N-API adopt). Call georo::initialize() first — a fresh CSGCompiler does not import geogram's argument groups. ---
classes.name: CSGCompiler

functions.//: --- booleans + self-intersections. GEO::mesh_union et al. are OVERLOADED (a flags variant and a bool-verbose one), so each entry names the signature it wants: ^^name is ill-formed for an overload set, and without the signature the FIRST-declared overload would be the flags one. Spelled GEO:: explicitly — the top-level namespace default qualifies the name, not the signature, which is spliced verbatim. ---

entries.name: mesh_union
entries.signature: void(GEO::Mesh&, const GEO::Mesh&, const GEO::Mesh&, bool)

entries.name: mesh_intersection
entries.signature: void(GEO::Mesh&, const GEO::Mesh&, const GEO::Mesh&, bool)

entries.name: mesh_difference
entries.signature: void(GEO::Mesh&, const GEO::Mesh&, const GEO::Mesh&, bool)
